correctness.rationale: Pairing opposite half-lines cancels the linear tilt term; integration gives 4+2(6!)β². The first-order factor at zero is 2(1−|x|), so zero is a strict cusp maximum at every finite tilt. Sign reflection reduces to b=|β|>0. With z=b|x|³ and s=+1 on the right, −1 on the left, the outward derivative has the sign of 6b^(1/3)z^(2/3)(z−s)−(z²−2sz+2). This excludes right-hand critical points for z≤1. On the remaining domains the positive level function H_s=(z²−2sz+2)/(6z^(2/3)(z−s)) diverges at both ends. Its logarithmic derivative is (z³−8z+4s)/(3z(z−s)(z²−2sz+2)); the cubic is negative at the lower endpoint and has only one increasing crossing afterward. Exact endpoint signs in the stated brackets are (−3/8,97/125) and (−1,991/1000). At a minimum level the outward derivative is negative off its isolated zero, so no new local maximum exists there; above the minimum there is exactly one outward + to − transition on that side. At z_L, H_R−H_L=(4−2z_L²)/(6z_L^(2/3)(z_L²−1))<0, establishing b_R<b_L. The independently evaluated thresholds agree with the displays. β=0 and positive location-scale transformations behave as stated. Dividing by β² gives pointwise convergence to x⁶e^(−|x|)/1440, a normalized density whose only maxima are ±6; Scheffé gives total variation. These arguments cover all parameters, rather than inferring them from plots or the frozen symbolic checker.
